clue.text: The fashion trade

definitions.meaning: the fashion is the prevailing usage or habit of the day
trade here is regular patronage given to a shop

explanation.surface: A one-line description of the clothing business.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: an accepted practice or usage, and the regular business a shopkeeper receives from patrons.

clue.text: Bridge-head?

parts.note: read not as a military foothold but as the head person on a ship's bridge

explanation.walkthrough: A bridgehead is a military foothold; split it and it is whoever is in charge on the bridge of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The commander of a vessel directs it from the bridge, so the ship's master is the bridge's head.

clue.text: Kind of western food that's long in the cooking

definitions.meaning: a cowboy film made cheaply in Italy, a genre named after Italian pasta

definitions.text: food that's long in the cooking
definitions.meaning: a pasta whose strands are long when boiled

explanation.surface: A remark about a dish that takes ages to prepare in the American West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long in the cooking' suggests slow preparation, but it means the pasta strands are long.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian-made cowboy films are known by the name of the long-stranded pasta.

clue.text: Giving an alternative sort of threat

definitions.meaning: a phrase meaning otherwise, offering another option
said at the end of a demand to warn of consequences

explanation.surface: Describing a warning that offers a choice.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means otherwise, and is also tacked on to a demand as a menacing warning.

clue.text: Big waves finally demolish old ships

definitions.meaning: large waves that crash and foam on the shore
ship-breaking yards and the workers in them scrap vessels at the end of their lives

explanation.surface: Heavy seas finishing off a fleet of aged vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Large crashing waves have this name, as do the yards and workers who scrap ships.

clue.text: Rebel king I turn to

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

indicators.note: turn tells us the little word to is flipped round to face the other way

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned

explanation.surface: An insurgent monarch announces that he is changing sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses TO to OT.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel and to run amok in a civil disturbance are close in sense as verbs of uprising.

clue.text: A diet put out for fitness

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of these three words are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A dieting regime abandoned in favour of getting fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitness for something means natural suitability or talent for it.

clue.text: Low interest rate due to unemployment perhaps

definitions.text: Low interest rate due to unemployment perhaps

parts.words: Low interest rate due to unemployment perhaps
parts.note: read not as banking but as a feeling of having little interest, as idleness may bring

explanation.walkthrough: The financial surface of the pink paper misleads: 'interest' is mental engagement, so a low level of it is boredom.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless boredom is a state of having little interest in anything, as can come with having no work.

clue.text: Staff held in a sort of respect

indicators.note: a sort of tells us the word respect is to be sorted into a different order

explanation.surface: An employee who is well regarded by the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees; it is a rod carried by a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial rod held by a monarch as an emblem of sovereignty is a staff held in the hand.

clue.text: A petition, common in book form

definitions.meaning: the Book of Common ... is the Anglican service book

explanation.surface: A formal request that is usually presented bound in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The Book of Common Prayer is the Church of England's traditional prayer book; the second definition alludes to its title.
explanation.definitionFit: A request made to God is a petition, and the Anglican service book is titled the Book of Common Prayer.

clue.text: Don't give up getting the unit back in shape

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other here

parts.note: a cone is a geometric shape

indicators.note: back tells us the word unit is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned

explanation.surface: Advice to persist while the team is restored to fitness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in shape' looks like being fit, but the shape is a geometric solid; 'back' reverses the unit word and 'in' sets it within that solid.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist or carry on is the opposite of quitting.

clue.text: Affected types from the Paris model agency

definitions.meaning: pretentious people who put on airs
in French the word for those who pose, such as models, is the same word

explanation.surface: Pretentious people sent by a French modelling firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word for one who poses, as a model does, is borrowed into English for a pretentious person.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentious people strike attitudes to impress, which is what the French borrowing literally describes.

clue.text: Attachment had noise coming from it

indicators.note: the answer comes from these letters rearranged, so the phrase signals an anagram of had noise

explanation.surface: A fitting that made a noise when it came loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesion is the act or state of sticking or being attached to something.

clue.text: Severe constriction at the centre

indicators.note: at the centre points to letters lying in the middle of the word constriction

explanation.surface: A tight narrowing in the middle of something is serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict and severe are synonyms for harsh or rigorous rules and people.

clue.text: Everybody agreed and calmed down

parts.note: everybody means all
to aye is to vote yes, so ayed means agreed

explanation.surface: A dispute in which the whole group came round and settled.
explanation.definitionFit: To allay fears is to quieten them, so the past tense means quietened or soothed.

clue.text: They may be eaten slowly or bolted

definitions.text: They may be eaten slowly or bolted

parts.words: They may be eaten slowly or bolted
parts.note: read not as gobbling food but as fasteners screwed on to bolts

explanation.walkthrough: 'bolted' suggests eating fast, but here these are hardware fastened onto bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: Kernels in shells are eaten as food, and threaded fasteners pair with bolts.

clue.text: Performance in which the middle section gets the twitch

definitions.text: Performance in which the middle section gets the twitch

parts.words: Performance in which the middle section gets the twitch
parts.note: read the middle section as the dancer's midriff, which shimmies and twitches

explanation.walkthrough: 'middle section' sounds like part of an orchestra or show; it is the abdomen.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern dance features rippling movements of the abdomen, the body's middle section.

clue.text: End a Metro trip to see it?

definitions.text: End a Metro trip to see it?

indicators.note: trip suggests stumbling, so the letters of these words fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A tourist finishing a ride on the Paris underground to visit a landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: The Paris Metro stops near the famous cathedral, so the whole clue is the instruction and the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris's Gothic cathedral is a sight that visitors take the Metro to see.

clue.text: Gather to see lambs gambolling

indicators.note: gambolling lambs leap about, so the letters of see lambs jump into a new order

explanation.surface: A crowd forming to watch young sheep frolic in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: To come together as a group is to gather or congregate.

clue.text: Wake up at the back?

parts.note: read wake not as rousing but as the trail of disturbed air behind a moving vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wake up' looks like rousing a sleeper; it is the turbulent trail behind a speeding vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The current of air behind a fast vehicle is its wake, which a following driver can use.

clue.text: Spit in the sea

parts.note: read spit not as saliva but as a narrow ridge of deposited sand in water

explanation.walkthrough: A spit is a narrow point of land or ridge of sand projecting into water.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge of sand built up by currents offshore is a geographical spit.

clue.text: Highlight of the Cresta Run

indicators.note: of the says the letters come out of the words Cresta Run

explanation.surface: The best moment of a famous toboggan course.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cresta Run is a toboggan run at St Moritz.
explanation.definitionFit: The star of a show is its main attraction or highlight.

clue.text: It's beaten by those who are themselves beaten

definitions.text: It's beaten by those who are themselves beaten

parts.words: It's beaten by those who are themselves beaten
parts.note: the idiom of beating a hasty withdrawal, done by a defeated army

explanation.walkthrough: To 'beat a retreat' is to withdraw, as losing troops do.
explanation.definitionFit: Defeated forces withdraw, and the idiom says they beat a withdrawal.

clue.text: Farewell words to the French about to meet death

indicators.note: about tells us the French phrase goes around the other piece

parts.note: aux is French for to the, before a plural
to meet death is to die

explanation.surface: Last goodbyes said to the French people by someone facing execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the French' is plural French for 'to the', and 'about' wraps it round the verb for meeting death; the plural French form is used in English too.
explanation.definitionFit: These are French goodbyes, the plural form used in English for formal leave-takings.

clue.text: Arrested outlaw sent back to bed

indicators.note: sent back tells us the word for outlaw is reversed

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A criminal is caught and returned to his bunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns BAN into NAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabbed is informal for caught or seized by the police.

clue.text: Sailor set up crime, seen in the dock

indicators.note: set up in a down entry tells us the sailor letters read upwards

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
a sin is an offence, a crime

explanation.surface: A sailor framed for an offence ends up in the dock in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns AB into BA in this down clue; 'the dock' is a harbour, not the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosed harbour area where ships are moored is a dock.

clue.text: A double-first

parts.note: read not as a top university degree but as two competitors finishing first together

explanation.walkthrough: A double first is a top Oxbridge degree in two subjects; here it is a race with two winners.
explanation.definitionFit: A race finish where two competitors tie for first place gives two winners.

clue.text: A shade too near the knuckle?

definitions.meaning: a colour, like that of the sky
British idiom for jokes that are close to indecent, risque

explanation.surface: A remark that is slightly too close to the bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near the knuckle' is a British idiom for close to indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour of a clear sky is a shade, and smutty jokes are called by the same colour.

clue.text: It's played for the HQ dance

parts.note: headquarters is a base
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Music performed for a party held at headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: This bat-and-ball sport is a game that people play.

clue.text: Underworld chief plays the ace

indicators.note: plays suggests the letters of these words are played around into a new order

explanation.surface: A gangland boss lays down his top card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld chief' suggests a crime boss, but it is a Greek goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, a goddess of witchcraft held sway in the realm of the dead.

clue.text: Submitted and faced the wall

definitions.meaning: handed in, as a bill or account
coated a wall with plaster or cement

explanation.surface: Someone gave in and was put up against the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faced the wall' suggests punishment, but it means coating it with plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is handed in, and a wall is coated with a first plaster layer.

clue.text: Expect disturbance in bar

indicators.note: disturbance tells us the letters of the word expect are disturbed into another order

explanation.surface: Anticipate trouble in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub; it is a preposition meaning apart from.
explanation.definitionFit: As prepositions, bar and except both mean apart from or excluding.
